source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which retinal cells are responsible for night vision?
questions.rationale: Rods: night vision; cones: color and bright light; macula: central vision.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anatomy of the Eye (PDF p. 472)
questions.quote: Rods - responsible for night vision

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A visual acuity of 20/200 means the client sees at 20 feet what a normal eye sees at:
questions.rationale: Top number is test distance; bottom is distance a normal eye sees the same line.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Snellen Chart (PDF p. 472)
questions.quote: A person whose vision is 20/200 can see an object from 20 feet away

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Normal intraocular pressure is:
questions.rationale: Tonometry measures IOP; normal 10–21 mm Hg.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tonometer (PDF p. 472)
questions.quote: Normal IOP is 10-21 mmHg

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which test screens for macular degeneration?
questions.rationale: Wavy or missing lines on the Amsler grid suggest macular problems.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Amsler Grid (PDF p. 473)
questions.quote: Test often used for patients with macular problems

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Legal blindness is best-corrected visual acuity of:
questions.rationale: Legal blindness: BCVA not exceeding 20/200 in the better eye.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Eye Terms (PDF p. 473)
questions.quote: Legal Blindness- BCVA that does not exceed 20/200

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Removal of the entire eye and part of the optic nerve is:
questions.rationale: Evisceration removes contents; exenteration removes eye, lids, and orbit contents.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Eye Terms (PDF p. 473)
questions.quote: Enucleation is the removal of the entire eye and part of the optic nerve

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should a client manage a stye?
questions.rationale: Warm soaks promote drainage; good hygiene; do not squeeze.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hordeolum (PDF p. 474)
questions.quote: Teach patient how to clean eyelid margins and not to squeeze the stye.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which compress is used for viral conjunctivitis?
questions.rationale: Cold compresses for viral; warm soaks for bacterial crusting.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Conjunctivitis (PDF p. 474)
questions.quote: Cold compress for viral conjunctivitis

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the most important measure to prevent spread of conjunctivitis?
questions.rationale: Good hand washing prevents spread.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Conjunctivitis (PDF p. 474)
questions.quote: Urge good hand washing to prevent spread of infection

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which test detects corneal abrasion?
questions.rationale: Fluorescein stains epithelial defects, seen with Wood's or slit lamp.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Corneal Abrasion (PDF p. 474)
questions.quote: Fluorescein staining

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with uveitis on topical corticosteroids should have follow-up for:
questions.rationale: Corticosteroids can increase IOP.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Iritis/Uveitis (PDF p. 475)
questions.quote: corticosteroids can increase I0P

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Gradual, painless blurring of vision with glare and a cloudy pupil suggests:
questions.rationale: Cataract: lens opacity, painless gradual loss, glare.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cataract (PDF p. 475)
questions.quote: Gradual and painless loss of vision

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After cataract surgery, which instruction is correct?
questions.rationale: Avoid bending, coughing, and straining; lie on unaffected side; wear shield.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cataract Nursing (PDF p. 476)
questions.quote: Advise patient against rapid movement or bending from the waist

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Sudden severe eye pain and restlessness after cataract surgery may indicate:
questions.rationale: Report sudden pain with restlessness and rising pulse.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cataract Nursing (PDF p. 476)
questions.quote: Notify health care provider of sudden pain associated with restlessness and increased pulse

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Sudden severe eye pain, halos, nausea, and a fixed semi-dilated pupil suggest:
questions.rationale: Acute angle closure is an emergency with very high IOP.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Glaucoma (PDF p. 477)
questions.quote: Pupil is vertically oval, fixed in a semi-dilated position

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Pilocarpine treats glaucoma by:
questions.rationale: Miotics constrict the pupil and open the trabecular meshwork for outflow.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Glaucoma Management (PDF p. 477)
questions.quote: topical miotic agents (increase the outflow of aqueous humor

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with glaucoma should avoid which drug class unless approved?
questions.rationale: Anticholinergics and corticosteroids may raise IOP.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Glaucoma Teaching (PDF p. 477)
questions.quote: avoid use of medications that may increase IOP, such as corticosteroids and anticholinergics

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding is typical of chronic open-angle glaucoma?
questions.rationale: Open-angle glaucoma: painless, progressive peripheral field loss.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Open-Angle Glaucoma (PDF p. 477)
questions.quote: Slowly developing impairment of peripheral vision

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with open-angle glaucoma feels fine and wants to stop eyedrops. The nurse explains:
options: Use is lifelong to prevent damage
questions.rationale: Glaucoma is chronic; IOP can damage the eye without symptoms.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Open-Angle Glaucoma Nursing (PDF p. 477)
questions.quote: although he may be asymptomatic, IOP could still be elevated

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Floaters and a curtain-like shadow across the visual field suggest:
questions.rationale: Retinal detachment: floaters, flashes, veil; surgical emergency.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Retinal Detachment (PDF p. 478)
questions.quote: A sensation of a veil-like coating may be present

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A silicone band placed around the sclera to reattach the retina is:
questions.rationale: Scleral buckle indents the sclera to bring retinal layers together.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Retinal Detachment Surgery (PDF p. 478)
questions.quote: Scleral Buckling
